cases.name: current-settings-permission-refusals
cases.covers: Current settings events, required permission hide/disable, shortcut refusals, command disablement and reset to registration defaults.

cases.name: capability-shape
cases.covers: The capability is workspace-scoped and exists from createKernel(); its members, in the object literal order; commands live in settings and a closure registry, with no session slice.

cases.name: registry
cases.covers: Config commands register in order; registerCommand appends and throws on a duplicate or an unparsable shortcut (registering nothing); its remover removes (a second call is a no-op), and re-registering moves an id to the end; hasCommand, listCommandIds and getMenuTarget read the registry.

cases.name: resolve-defaults
cases.covers: With no i18n and no shell, a command resolves to its labelKey verbatim, enabled and visible, not active, with no accent, categories [] and its shortcuts as written; a missing id resolves to null. Surface targets without a shell are inactive.

cases.name: derivations
cases.covers: resolve() calls active, then iconAccent, then enabled, then visible, each with a CommandCtx bound to the explicit document, else the active one (null with none open, and an empty string is kept); their answers land on the resolved command.

cases.name: throwing-derivations-fall-back
cases.covers: A derivation that throws falls back: enabled and visible to true, active to false, iconAccent to none. The command still resolves, and execute still runs it.

cases.name: icon-accent
cases.covers: iconAccent carries what the derivation returns: both colours or one; empty, null and undefined mean no accent; a throw means no accent; an absent derivation is never called.

cases.name: categories
cases.covers: config.disabledCategories seeds settings; a disabled category hides and disables its command without invoking enabled/visible; idempotent changes fire nothing; execute refuses a hidden command.

cases.name: i18n-labels
cases.covers: With i18n present the label resolves the command id then labelKey through current and fallback locale; a missing key falls back to the command id and warns once; search matches the translated label.

cases.name: shell-derived-active
cases.covers: Without an active override, a menu command is active while its menu is open, a panel (string or object) or modal command while its surface is open; a menu wins over a panel, a panel over a modal; an empty menu or modal id is no target, an empty panel id is one; an active derivation overrides the shell; the shell is the target document's.

cases.name: execute-routing
cases.covers: Without run, execute routes a surface target through the target document's shell: toggleMenu for a menu, toggle with the panel's exclusive tag (or none), toggle exclusive "modal" for a modal; a menu wins over a panel and a panel over a modal; empty menu and modal ids are no target. Without a shell, or a target, nothing happens.

cases.name: execute-guards-and-run
cases.covers: execute resolves first (every derivation runs), then refuses a disabled or hidden command with a rejected result; otherwise it calls run with a fresh CommandCtx and skips the surface routing. It awaits the run: a run that throws or rejects makes execute reject with an operation-failed PluginError, and a pending run keeps execute pending until it settles.

cases.name: command-ctx
cases.covers: What a command function can do with its CommandCtx: get resolves a document-scoped token for the target document and throws the kernel's refusal when it cannot; tryGet answers null instead; workspace tokens resolve whatever the target; an empty target falls back to the active document; documentId and the Documents capability expose the current document and list.

cases.name: follows-the-active-document
cases.covers: An unaddressed resolve or execute binds to whichever document is active at the call, and to none once the last one closes.

cases.name: search
cases.covers: search trims and lowercases the query, then keeps visible commands, in registry order, whose lowercased label contains it or whose id (not lowercased) does; an empty query keeps every visible command; every command is resolved, hidden ones included.

cases.name: match-stroke
cases.covers: matchStroke returns the first command, in registry order, any of whose shortcuts matches the stroke on the given platform, and null when none does; it ignores enablement. The palette is registered last through the capability, so its remover can take it out.

cases.name: registered-functions
cases.covers: A command registered through the capability carries its functions like a configured one: derivations and run are called with the CommandCtx.

cases.name: re-entrant-registry
cases.covers: A command function may use the commands capability itself: a run that executes another command, and a visible derivation that, mid-search, removes a command not yet visited and registers a new one; the second time, the registration is a duplicate. Commands a derivation removes are registered through the capability by a setup command, which keeps their removers.

cases.name: unregister-behind-a-search
cases.covers: A derivation that removes a command the search already visited changes nothing about the rest of the walk: every later command is still visited once. The commands are registered by a setup command, which keeps the remover of `a`.

cases.name: register-many-shortcuts-and-can-execute
cases.covers: registerCommands registers each definition in order and returns one remover for all of them (a definition replaced since is left alone); replace: true swaps a definition in place of a duplicate. listShortcuts lists every binding in registry order. canExecute is enabled and visible for the target, false for a missing id.

cases.name: execute-events
cases.covers: onExecuted fires after a command ran, with its id, target document and the args as given; onExecutionFailed fires when run throws or rejects, with the failure as PluginErrorInfo, and execute rejects with the mapped PluginError. The run sees the args on its CommandCtx. A refused command fires neither. A throwing listener is reported and its siblings still fire; after unsubscribing nothing fires.

cases.name: get-and-list-commands
cases.covers: getCommand hands back the definition as registered (null for an unknown id); listCommands resolves every command in registry order for the target document.

cases.name: a-bad-config-refuses-the-kernel
cases.covers: Configured duplicate ids resolve to the last definition in the first insertion position; runtime registration still refuses duplicates.

cases.name: a-bad-config-shortcut-refuses-the-kernel
cases.covers: An unparsable shortcut in config.commands makes the first configured-registry read throw the parse error.

cases.name: after-destroy
cases.covers: Retained registrations and definition-only reads survive teardown; operations resolving the active document refuse through the destroyed kernel. Settings writes are dropped, and removers retain their registration identity.
